arguments.summary: Technical assessment through the 2026-09-22 completed session: ANET showed strong absolute returns at 5, 21 and 63 sessions. Relative performance was positive versus SPY at 5/21/63 sessions, while versus XLK it was slightly negative at 5 sessions but positive at 21 and 63 sessions. Price was above rising short-, medium- and long-term averages and near the prior 21-session closing high, but 63-session realized volatility and drawdown show substantial path risk. Historical regime-conditioned positive-return frequencies were below unconditional base rates at every requested horizon; these overlapping, dependent analogs are not calibrated forecasts. The technical setup is therefore a conditional opportunity, with longer-window leadership but no claim of sector leadership over the latest five sessions.

claims.text: As of the 2026-09-22 completed session, ANET closed at $205.19. Split-adjusted price returns were +6.4043% over 5 sessions, +8.7676% over 21 sessions and +26.5043% over 63 sessions. The close was 4.9533% above SMA20 ($195.506), 8.9237% above SMA50 ($188.3796) and 31.6234% above SMA200 ($155.89175). Realized volatility was 22.4371%, 44.8032% and 55.0458% over the respective 5/21/63-session measurements, and drawdown from the 252-session high was -2.5226%. These are completed-session observations, not intrinsic-value or forecast signals.

Matched-date, SIP-feed, split-adjusted price-return comparisons as of 2026-09-22:
PAIR ANET/SPY 5=+4.2931 21=+7.7672 63=+21.0789
PAIR ANET/XLK 5=-0.4151 21=+1.6976 63=+19.9459
ANET therefore outperformed SPY over each of the 5-, 21- and 63-session windows. Against XLK, ANET underperformed by 0.4151 percentage points over 5 sessions, then outperformed by 1.6976 points over 21 sessions and 19.9459 points over 63 sessions. The sign reversal against XLK permits a recent sector-relative pause to coexist with medium- and mandate-horizon leadership.

The path panel shows ANET's SMA20 increased 1.7405% over the latest five sessions, while the last close remained 0.1120% below the prior 21-session closing high. Latest-session volume was 0.9790 times the preceding 20-session median, although average volume over the latest five sessions was 1.3676 times that median. Maximum close-path drawdown within the 63-session window was -15.5060%. This supports a rebound/continuation interpretation but not a confirmed breakout: the prior closing high had not been cleared, the latest volume was near its prior median, and the observed path contained a sizable reversal.

The current historical regime is close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50 and positive 21-session return. At 5 sessions, the conditional positive-return frequency was 55.4517% (178 positive observations among 321), median +0.4974%, and 10th/90th percentiles -7.5762%/+6.7425%; the unconditional base rate was 58.6207% (374/638), median +1.1988%, and 10th/90th percentiles -7.5914%/+9.7238%. At 21 sessions, conditional frequency was 63.8629% (205/321), median +2.8939%, and 10th/90th percentiles -12.6204%/+15.5652%; unconditional frequency was 68.3386% (436/638), median +4.7772%, and 10th/90th percentiles -12.4354%/+19.9845%. At 63 sessions, conditional frequency was 65.7321% (211/321), median +10.6427%, and 10th/90th percentiles -20.6472%/+36.7049%; unconditional frequency was 75.3918% (481/638), median +13.4654%, and 10th/90th percentiles -12.5658%/+41.4201%. These are historical empirical frequencies from one finite 2023-12-05 to 2026-06-23 lookback. Forward windows overlap and observations are dependent, so the figures are not calibrated forecast probabilities, causal estimates or guarantees. A change in any regime sign would invalidate the current conditional comparison and require recomputation.

For the 63-session mandate, the strongest continuation case is preservation of the positive 21- and 63-session excess-return signs versus both SPY and XLK, combined with price holding above the frozen SMA20 checkpoint and eventually clearing the prior 21-session closing high on repeated volume support. The opposing interpretation is an extended rebound: ANET slightly lagged XLK over 5 sessions, latest-session volume was near its preceding median, 63-session realized volatility was 55.0458%, and maximum close-path drawdown over that window was -15.5060%. Thus the price-level uptrend and longer-window relative leadership are supported, but low-risk persistence and 5-session sector leadership are not.

The fixed external references were mixed and are not watchlist breadth. SPY returned +2.1112%, +1.0004% and +5.4254% over 5/21/63 sessions; IWM returned +0.7260%, -4.2506% and -2.7462%; HYG returned +0.3700%, -1.1808% and -1.5024%. These provide broad-equity, small-cap and high-yield context only and do not establish news causality for ANET.

gaps.description: Stronger continuation evidence would require subsequent completed closes above the then-prior 21-session closing high with sustained multi-session volume, plus a recomputed out-of-sample or non-overlapping regime study. The supplied 638 historical starting points use overlapping forward windows from one finite history, so independence, persistence and calibrated forecast probability are not established.

assumptions: All relative comparisons use the same 2026-09-22 completed-session cutoff, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices and price-return convention.
The $195.506 review threshold is the frozen SMA20 observed on 2026-09-22, not a future dynamic moving average and not an order level.
Relative-leadership conclusions are descriptive and must be recomputed after additional completed sessions; they are separate from valuation and fundamental conclusions.
arguments.counter_thesis: The positive price-level trend and 21-/63-session leadership may be a late-stage rebound rather than durable continuation. ANET had already gained 26.5043% over 63 sessions, experienced a 15.5060% close-path drawdown within that window, remained just below the prior 21-session closing high, and underperformed XLK by 0.4151 percentage points over the latest five sessions. A close below the frozen SMA20 checkpoint plus negative recomputed 21-session excess returns versus both SPY and XLK would shift the interpretation toward fading momentum. A negative 63-session excess-return sign versus either benchmark would invalidate longer-window leadership against that benchmark.

review_conditions.description: Research checkpoint: a completed split-adjusted close below the frozen 2026-09-22 SMA20 level of $195.506 before expiry would weaken the positive price-level trend and increase the relevance of the observed -15.5060% 63-session drawdown path. This is a frozen analytical threshold, not a future dynamic average or trade instruction.

Recompute matched 21- and 63-session ANET excess price returns versus SPY and XLK after new completed sessions. If both 21-session signs become negative, downgrade the medium-window leadership reading to a fading rebound. If either 63-session sign becomes negative, invalidate longer-window leadership against that benchmark. Persistently positive 21- and 63-session signs, especially after a completed close above the then-prior 21-session closing high with sustained multi-session volume, would strengthen the continuation case.
